injuryReports.name: DeMario Douglas
injuryReports.returnComment: The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.

injuryReports.name: Hunter Henry
injuryReports.returnComment: Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.

injuryReports.name: Mack Hollins
injuryReports.returnComment: In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.
injuryReports.injury: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.

injuryReports.name: Corey Kiner
injuryReports.returnComment: Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.
injuryReports.injury: Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit.

injuryReports.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
injuryReports.returnComment: The whole Patriots' offense struggled after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, but Stevenson also didn't look to be in peak form after dealing with a knee issue during the practice week. Corey Kiner wound up leading the backfield with just 25 rushing yards on 10 totes. Stevenson will get a Week 11 bye to rest up, and if Maye's injury ends up sidelining him for an extended period, New England could lean heavily on its running game in Week 12 against the Chargers.
injuryReports.injury: Stevenson carried the ball six times for four yards and caught his only target for one yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.

injuryReports.name: Dre'Mont Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.
injuryReports.injury: Undisclosed

injuryReports.name: Robert Spillane
injuryReports.returnComment: Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Asim Richards
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: David Edwards
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Juwan Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson was listed as having both hamstring and wrist injuries. He injured the hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Bears but this is the first report of a wrist issue. Head coach Kellen Moore said that Johnson is "day-to-day," according to Terrell. If Johnson does not progress in time for Sunday's game, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp would be the Saints' primary tight end options.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jonas Sanker
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanker was able to wrap up Caleb Williams for the first sack of his career in Week 11, and he collected seven-plus tackles for the fifth time this year. He'll probably be spending more time in coverage against a pass-dependent Bengals offense in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Sanker recorded seven tackles (four solo) including 1.0 sacks during Sunday's 21-13 loss at Chicago.

injuryReports.name: Danny Stutsman
injuryReports.returnComment: Stutsman found himself in the right place at the right time when a Caleb Williams pass was batted into the air late in the second quarter, but the Saints weren't able to capitalize after starting in Bears territory. He also logged nine total tackles for a second straight game. His role in Week 12 against the Bengals will likely depend heavily on the status of Pete Werner (hamstring).
injuryReports.injury: Stutsman recorded nine tackles (three solo) and an interception during Sunday's 21-13 loss at Chicago.

injuryReports.name: Oscar Delp
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie third-round pick out of Georgia has handled a muted role at tight end behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant this season, compiling five receptions for 26 yards on five targets through nine appearances. Delp was limited to just 21 of the Saints' 72 offensive snaps in Week 11, but he could see his playing time pick up if the hamstring injury that knocked Johnson out of Sunday's loss early prevents him from suiting up this coming weekend in Cincinnati.
injuryReports.injury: Delp hauled in his lone target for a six-yard reception in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Pete Werner
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Erik McCoy
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Biceps

injuryReports.name: Martin Emerson Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Taliese Fuaga
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Kaden Elliss
injuryReports.returnComment: The five tackles were Elliss's fewest in a game this season, and it comes after back-to-back games of double-digit stops. Across seven appearances in 2026, Elliss has produced 61 tackles (31 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass breakups on 100 percent of the defensive snaps in those seven contests.
injuryReports.injury: Elliss recorded five tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Lance
injuryReports.returnComment: Lance was unable to reel in a deep pass from quarterback Tyler Shough in the first quarter, and he didn't get another look the rest of the game. The wide receiver was on the field for 21 offensive snaps, ranking fourth at his position behind Devaughn Vele (64), Chris Olave (62) and Jordyn Tyson (36) in the contest. Lance will continue to primarily serve as a special-teams asset for New Orleans moving forward, making him an unattractive option for fantasy managers.
injuryReports.injury: Lance failed to catch his only target and added 47 yards on kickoff returns during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: CJ Donaldson
injuryReports.returnComment: Donaldson recorded season highs in both catches and targets, and he finished third on the Saints in both of those categories behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. However, Donaldson coughed up the football on his first catch of the game early in the second quarter, which the Bears offense capitalized on with a six-play drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown pass from Caleb Williams to D'Andre Swift. Donaldson's 32 offensive snaps were tied with Travis Etienne for most among Saints running backs Sunday, although Etienne saw a heavier workload with 14 carries for 76 yards while Alvin Kamara, who played only eight offensive snaps, found the end zone on a one-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough in the second quarter. Losers of three of their last four games, the Saints will look to reverse their fortunes in Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Donaldson logged a five-yard carry and brought in all four of his targets for 12 yards during the Saints' 21-13 loss to the Bears on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Noah Fant
injuryReports.returnComment: Fant played 49 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The starting tight end was on the field for 69 percent of the team's offensive plays but remains off the same page with quarterback Tyler Shough. The tight end's five targets are the most attention he has seen since Week 1 against the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Fant caught two of his five targets for 19 yards in the Saints' 21-13 loss to the Bears on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Charlie Smyth
injuryReports.returnComment: The Saints didn't have a scoring drive until the second quarter, when Smyth made his season-long, 56-yard field goal to cut the lead going into halftime, his first of two 50-plus-yard FGs in the game. The 25-year-old also continued his perfect PAT percentage for the season, making his singular attempt (5-for-5 in three games). His play on kickoffs stood out Sunday, committing two penalties for kicking the ball out of bounds and giving Chicago excellent field position.
injuryReports.injury: Smyth made two of three field-goal attempts and his lone PAT in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Alvin Kamara
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran running back played just eight of 72 offensive snaps, while both CJ Donaldson and Travis Etienne played 32 each with Audric Estime a healthy inactive. Kamara has touched the ball just seven times on 24 snaps over the past two weeks, but he's turned three of those touches into short touchdowns. The Saints' three-man backfield continues to be one to try and avoid when making fantasy lineup decisions. Kamara's proverbial gas tank is nearing empty, but the Saints continue to give him high-value touches near the goal line while refusing to play him outside of the red zone.
injuryReports.injury: Kamara rushed one time for one yard and caught a one-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Devaughn Vele
injuryReports.returnComment: Vele continues to run virtually every route for New Orleans, and the seven grabs matched his season high from Week 1 against the Lions, while Vele's 76 yards are a new high-water mark for the receiver. It was notable that Jordyn Tyson ran just 22 routes on Tyler Shough's 51 dropbacks against Chicago. The Saints offense has become tough to predict on a week-to-week basis. Vele is more of a low-ceiling fantasy WR4/5 most weeks.
injuryReports.injury: Vele caught seven passes for 76 yards on seven targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Jordyn Tyson
injuryReports.returnComment: One week after logging 13 targets as Tyler Shough's top downfield option, Tyson all but disappeared as Chris Olave instead saw WR1-worthy volume. The Saints' aerial attack simply may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game, which would mark Tyson as a volatile, but high-ceiling, fantasy asset for the rest of the season. The rookie will try to bounce back in Week 12 against the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Tyson caught one of two targets for six yards and added four rushing yards on his only carry in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The former Jaguar was the clear No. 1 option in the backfield for the Saints. Alvin Kamara saw just two touches and CJ Donaldson handled five, although Kamara did vulture another red-zone TD on a one-yard reception in the second quarter, Most of Etienne's production came on a 46-yard scamper that saw him tackled just short of the goal line, setting up Kamara's score, but the fact that he was able to produce his first big play as a Saint was still encouraging. Etienne will attempt to build on this performance in Week 12 against the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Etienne carried the ball 14 times for 76 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 21-13 loss to Chicago.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Shough
injuryReports.returnComment: Despite the high volume of attempts, Shough couldn't get much going through the air while dealing with a ferocious Chicago pass rush that sacked him six times, including one for a fourth-quarter safety by Montez Sweat. Shough has gone four straight games without producing multiple TDs, posting a 4:3 TD:INT over that stretch while completing 67.3 percent of his passes with a weak 6.3 YPA. The second-year QB will likely need to be a lot more productive in Week 12 if the Saints are going to keep up with Joe Burrow and the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Shough completed 25 of 42 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears. He added 34 rushing yards on three carries.

injuryReports.name: Chris Olave
injuryReports.returnComment: One week after taking a back seat to rookie Jordyn Tyson, Olave re-emerged as Tyler Shough's favorite downfield option, as he set a new season high in targets and topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time in 2026. Tyson, meanwhile, caught only one pass on two targets, suggesting the Saints' aerial attack may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game. Olave will look to make an impact again in Week 12 against the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Olave caught nine of 15 targets for 102 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Zach Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: As the emergency QB3, Wilson is not allowed to play Sunday unless starter Tyler Shough and backup Spencer Rattler both leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection. Wilson has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Bears on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Audric Estime
injuryReports.returnComment: Estime's role in the offense was reduced in Week 10 against the Panthers, which marked Travis Etienne's return from a five-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Estime is a healthy scratch for Sunday's game, which means Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson will operate as the rotational options out of the backfield behind Etienne. Estime's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Estime (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Dru Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Arvell Reese
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Likely
injuryReports.returnComment: Likely pops up on the injury report to begin the week as the Giants prepare for their matchup against the Colts on Sunday. He practiced in limited fashion but was held back from a full session. Provided Likely can ramp up to a full practice later in the week, he should be ready for Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Shelby Harris
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Chris Manhertz
injuryReports.returnComment: The second-quarter reception was the first of the season for Manhertz, who had suited up for each of the Giants' previous nine games but was targeted just once. While taking the field for 19 of the Giants' 70 offensive snaps, Manhertz finished a distant second to Isaiah Likely (53 snaps) among the team's tight ends. Manhertz is expected to operate mostly as a blocker on offense while being a mainstay on the Giants' special-teams units.
injuryReports.injury: Mahertz secured his lone target for a 14-yard reception in Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Abdul Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter was able to notch his first career multi-sack performance, getting to Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence in both the first and second quarters. The edge rusher registered 12 total pressures in the contest according to NFL Next Gen Stats, and he has now compiled 26 total tackles (10 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and a forced fumble over 10 games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Deonte Banks
injuryReports.returnComment: Banks matched his season high in tackles while and was able to secure his second interception of the season, jumping in front of a short pass from Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter. The cornerback has now registered 33 total tackles (21 solo) and a career-high 14 passes defensed, including two interceptions, while also scoring a defensive touchdown over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Banks recorded six total tackles (five solo) and three passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Dawuane Smoot
injuryReports.returnComment: Smoot was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster for three consecutive weeks between Weeks 9 and 11, and he accumulated three tackles (one solo), including 1.0 sacks, in that span. Now that he's on the active roster, Smoot will be available for the Giants for the rest of the season while serving in a rotational role at the edge rusher position behind Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux.
injuryReports.injury: The Giants signed Smoot off the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Greg Newsome II
injuryReports.returnComment: Newsome is expected to undergo surgery for a sprained ankle that he sustained in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. Now that he's on IR, Newsome will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Lions on Monday, Dec. 28. Paulson Adebo is expected to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside cornerback in Newsome's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Micah McFadden
injuryReports.returnComment: With Tremaine Edmunds (chest) done for the season, McFadden has started each of the last four games as an every-down linebacker. During that span, he's piled up 36 tackles (23 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: McFadden recorded seven tackles (three solo) in Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Devin Singletary
injuryReports.returnComment: The running back played just 10 offensive snaps behind starter Cam Skattebo. Singletary has averaged just 2.9 yards per carry this year on 41 attempts.
injuryReports.injury: Singletary finished with one carry for five yards and one catch for five yards in Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Darnell Mooney
injuryReports.returnComment: Quarterback J.J. McCarthy was inefficient against a solid Jaguars defense in Week 11, completing just 18 of his 38 pass attempts for 173 yards. A couple of those 20 incompletions were intended for an open Mooney, who continued to operate in the deeper areas of the field. He'll keep hunting for a big play in Week 12 at Indianapolis.
injuryReports.injury: Mooney did not catch any of his five targets during Sunday's 23-18 win versus the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Theo Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson was third in offensive snaps (14) among Giants tight ends Sunday behind starter Isaiah Likely (49) and veteran Chris Manhertz (19). With that said, Johnson did manage to record at least one catch for the fourth time in his last five games. As long as Likely remains available, though, Johnson will remain in a rotational role.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson caught his only target for 15 yards during Sunday's 23-18 win versus the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Malachi Fields
injuryReports.returnComment: Fields played 56 offensive snaps in the contest, logging 86 percent of the Giants' such plays. Despite the lack of catches, the No. 2 wide receiver continues to receive attention from quarterback J.J. McCarthy on a week-to-week basis.
injuryReports.injury: Fields caught two of his five targets for 25 yards in the Giants' 23-15 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dominic Zvada
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie kicker continues to have his ups and downs. While he was good from 53, 54 and 43 yards, Zvada missed a chip shot from 32 yards on the opening drive of the second half that left coach John Harbaugh shaking his head. Zvada continues to be a bit of a liability, as he's made just 11 of 18 field-goal attempts over his last six games. Harbaugh is clearly growing more frustrated by the week, and it could lead to the Giants making a move at the position.
injuryReports.injury: Zvada made three of four field-goal attempts and both PATs in Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: J.J. McCarthy
injuryReports.returnComment: McCarthy had his share of trouble against an aggressive Jaguars defense, leading to a season-worst 47.4 percent completion rate. However, the emerging signal-caller avoided turnovers and connected with Malik Nabers for an eight-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter. McCarthy also provided some timely contributions with his legs, and he's averaging 5.4 yards on his 22 rush attempts to date. McCarthy connected with nine different targets overall as he continues to show good command of the offense, and he'll look to bounce back efficiency-wise in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: McCarthy completed 18 of 38 passes for 173 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions and rushed seven times for 33 yards in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Cam Skattebo
injuryReports.returnComment: Skattebo was unsurprisingly stymied on the ground by the Jaguars' elite run defense, and he couldn't really make up for it with his work through the air. Skattebo also committed another untimely turnover, fumbling at Jacksonville's 31-yard line with just over four minutes remaining in the third quarter and New York trying to add to a 20-6 lead. The change of possession ultimately didn't lead to any Jaguars points, however, and head coach John Harbaugh showed some faith in the second-year back by affording him the opportunity to ice the upset win with three carries on the final drive. Skattebo proved up to the task by netting 13 yards on those touches to force the Jags to exhaust their timeouts, and he should continue helming the backfield in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Skattebo rushed 14 times for 34 yards and brought in three of seven targets for 14 yards in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Malik Nabers
injuryReports.returnComment: Nabers was in the familiar position of leading the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and the third-year star also snapped a four-game touchdown drought with an eight-yard grab in the second quarter. Nabers has at least five catches in eight straight contests and three double-digit target tallies within that span, and the 2024 first-round pick should continue to be the subject of plenty of J.J. McCarthy's attention in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Nabers brought in seven of 12 targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: T'Vondre Sweat
injuryReports.returnComment: The defensive lineman was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Sweat hasn't played since Week 7 and has logged 17 tackles (five solo) across 229 defensive snaps this season.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Though Williams and fellow wideout Omar Cooper (ankle/groin) were both sidelined for the Jets' Week 11 win over the Chargers, the former appears to be in a better spot on the health front to begin Week 12. Williams was able to take some reps in Wednesday's walkthrough session, while Cooper was a spectator. If he's able to play Sunday in Miami and if Cooper remains out for another game, Williams could end up serving as the Jets' No. 3 wideout behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell.
injuryReports.injury: Ribs

injuryReports.name: Joseph Ossai
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Dylan Parham
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Harrison Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie wide receiver will be sidelined for a fourth consecutive practice while he continues to manage a pair of injuries, but the Jets aren't closing the door on Cooper putting an end to a one-game absence and playing this Sunday in Miami. In order to put himself in a position to suit up this weekend, however, Cooper will likely need to put in a full practice either Thursday or Friday. If Cooper ends up missing another game, the likes of Adonai Mitchell, Isaiah Williams (ribs), Tim Patrick and practice-squad member Sterling Shepard could be in line for added snaps and targets.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jeremy Ruckert
injuryReports.returnComment: Since recording eight catches for 48 yards and a touchdown over the Jets' first three games, Ruckert has yet to draw a target in any of the team's subsequent eight contests. Ruckert's downturn in involvement in the passing game coincides with the Jets' top two tight ends -- Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq -- getting back to full health after they were either limited or sidelined in the early part of the season.
injuryReports.injury: Ruckert went without a target while logging 16 of the Jets' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Beck
injuryReports.returnComment: The 30-year-old Beck has been one of the more versatile players in the league this season. In addition to taking snaps as a fullback and tight end, Beck often serves as a short-kickoff specialist for the Jets and while also contributing on the special teams coverage and return units. While the variety of roles he handles makes him valuable from a real-life standpoint, Beck maintains little fantasy relevance. He's carried twice for one yard and has yet to draw a target through the Jets' first 11 games.
injuryReports.injury: Beck played all but one of his 13 snaps on special teams in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Demario Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the second consecutive week in which Davis posted six stops, and he finished Sunday's game tied for the second-most tackles on the Jets behind Jamien Sherwood (11). Davis is up to 74 total tackles through 11 regular-season games, and the 2012 third-rounder is well on pace to record his 10th-straight 100-tackle season.
injuryReports.injury: Davis registered six tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dane Belton
injuryReports.returnComment: Belton played every single defensive snap Sunday and finished tied for the second-most tackles on the Jets behind Jamien Sherwood (11). Belton has recorded at least six stop in 10 of 11 regular-season games and is up to 88 tackles (42 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and five pass defenses. He is well on his way to cracking the tackling century mark for a second consecutive season.
injuryReports.injury: Belton posted six tackles (one solo) during the Jets' 27-24 win over the Chargers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: David Bailey
injuryReports.returnComment: Week 11 was the third multi-sack performance of the season for Bailey, and his first takedown of Justin Herbert early in the second quarter resulted in a fumble that the Chargers recovered. Bailey is up to 9.5 sacks through 10 regular-season games, which leads all  rookies and is tied for third-most in the NFL behind Will Anderson (11.5) and Greg Rousseau (10.0). Bailey also leads the league with six forced fumbles, and the Texas Tech product is living up to his pedigree as the second-overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft.
injuryReports.injury: Bailey recorded five tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble during the Jets' 27-24 win over the Chargers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jamien Sherwood
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the linebacker's fourth game this season with double-digit tackles. He also had a fourth-quarter sack wiped off the board by a Jets penalty. Through 11 games this season, Sherwood has recorded 97 tackles (49 solo), four pass breakups, three forced fumbles and a fumble recovery on 97 percent of the defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Sherwood recorded 11 tackles (eight solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Sterling Shepard
injuryReports.returnComment: Shepard was elevated for Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers due to the absences of fellow wideouts Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs). The veteran receiver answered the call by hauling in both of his targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Since Shepard has now been elevated the maximum three times, he'll need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up again for the Jets this season.
injuryReports.injury: Shepard reverted to the Jets' practice squad Monday.

injuryReports.name: Jason Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanders got the scoring started with a 50-yard field goal to cap the opening drive of the game. He later made one from 24 yards in the third quarter. Sanders has been a bright spot for the Jets this season, as he entered play Sunday leading the league in field-goal attempts (28) and makes (25), and he further boosted his conversion rate. The Jets have struggled to turn red-zone possessions into touchdowns this season, making Sanders a valuable fantasy kicker.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders made both of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Mason Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: The Jets controlled this game from start to finish and never trailed, so Geno Smith attempted just 21 passes to 37 run plays for New York. Taylor's 25 yards were his most in a game since Week 7, and he's totaled just 10 catches for 75 yards and no touchdowns over his last four contests. He's a very risky play as a fantasy tight end.
injuryReports.injury: Taylor caught two passes for 25 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: As has been the case for three straight weeks, with Breece Hall back healthy, Davis has been glued to special teams for the Jets. He has no fantasy appeal.
injuryReports.injury: Davis didn't play an offensive snap in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Kenyon Sadiq
injuryReports.returnComment: Sadiq finished tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and running back Breece Hall behind wideout Garrett Wilson (five). The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for just the second time since catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a score in Week 3 against the Lions. Sadiq has now caught 25 of 36 targets for 268 yards and a score while adding a three-yard rushing touchdown over the first 11 regular-season contests of his career.
injuryReports.injury: Sadiq caught all three of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Adonai Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) inactive, Mitchell's role didn't change, as his three targets tied with two other teammates for second on the team behind Garrett Wilson's five on a day the Jets called 37 run plays to just 22 passes. Mitchell has just one touchdown this season and has only 14 catches for 212 yards and no touchdowns in six games surrounding his 7-142-1 receiving performance from Week 8 against the Raiders. He's a big-play specialist in an offense that prefers to feed Wilson and its running backs.
injuryReports.injury: Mitchell caught two passes for 30 yards on three targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Braelon Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen's 16 carries matched his total from the previous two games combined, as he had seen a downtick in opportunities since fellow RB Breece Hall returned from a quadriceps injury. Hall led the backfield once again with 100 scrimmage yards and a touchdown on 23 touches, but Allen was a key part of the game plan as well in the run-heavy win. The Jets will face a one-win team for a second consecutive game in Week 12 at Miami, which could allow Allen to stay involved alongside Hall.
injuryReports.injury: Allen rushed 16 times for 75 yards while catching his lone target for nine yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Geno Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith didn't have a completion longer than 21 yards but kept the offense on schedule with an accurate performance. Most importantly, he stepped up in the red zone, which has been the team's Achilles' heel throughout the season. Smith threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to Breece Hall to snap the Jets' two-game touchdown drought in the second quarter, then tacked on touchdown passes of eight and 15 yards to practice-squad elevation Sterling Shepard. The veteran QB will take a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 12 road game against the Dolphins, who defeated the Jets in Week 7 despite three touchdown passes from Smith.
injuryReports.injury: Smith completed 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. He also rushed once for four yards.

injuryReports.name: Garrett Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson led the team in receiving yards and targets as Geno Smith threw for just 176 yards, though Wilson wasn't on the receiving end of any of Smith's three touchdown passes. The Jets' No. 1 wideout hasn't scored since Week 5, and Wilson has fallen short of 45 receiving yards four times this season, though he has also topped 100 yards three times. Wilson will face a Dolphins defense in Week 12 that held him to a season-low 26 receiving yards in their Week 7 meeting.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson caught three of five targets for 39 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Arnold Ebiketie
injuryReports.returnComment: After his trade to the Bengals fell through two weeks ago, Ebiketie is now dealing with an injury that will sideline him for at least one contest. Jalyx Hunt and A.J. Epenesa should soak up extra snaps off the edge for the Eagles.
injuryReports.injury: Oblique

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: The cornerback was injured in last Sunday's win over the Steelers. With Jones set to miss Thanksgiving Day against Dallas, Riq Woolen and Kelee Ringo are likely to see increased snaps opposite Quinyon Mitchell.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Quinyon Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: The star cornerback was injured in last Sunday's win over the Steelers, but the couple days of rest was enough for him to be available for Thanksgiving Day in Dallas. Mitchell has started all 10 games this season, producing 41 tackles (32 solo) and 11 pass breakups, including his first career interception. He should see plenty of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on Thursday.
injuryReports.injury: Mitchell (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday's game against the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Will Shipley
injuryReports.returnComment: Despite being listed as a limited participant throughout the week, Shipley made enough improvement in his recovery from an illness and his lingering plantar fascia injury to get the green light to play Thanksgiving Day. Shipley is expected to contribute as a kickoff returner along with serving as the top backup out of the backfield to Saquon Barkley. In his return from a four-game stint on injured reserve during last week's win over the Steelers, Shipley carried four times for nine yards while playing 19 of 53 snaps on offense.
injuryReports.injury: Shipley (illness/foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday's game against the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Tanner McKee
injuryReports.returnComment: McKee was estimated to be a limited participant on Monday's injury report due to an injury to his ribs. He now looks to be all set to serve as the team's primary reserve option at quarterback behind starter Joe Milton on Thursday against the Cowboys.
injuryReports.injury: McKee (ribs) was a full participant at the Eagles' walkthrough practice Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Dallas Goedert
injuryReports.returnComment: Philadelphia deemed Goedert a limited participant on Monday's estimated injury report, but had the team held a traditional practice Tuesday, the veteran tight end would have been able to increase his activity. Goedert thus looks on track to play Thursday, when he'll face off against a Cowboys defense that he burned for five receptions for 48 yards on seven targets back in Week 7.
injuryReports.injury: The Eagles listed Goedert (shin) as a full participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.

injuryReports.name: Saquon Barkley
injuryReports.returnComment: Though Tuesday's injury report was merely an estimate, Barkley would have been able to take every rep had the Eagles held a traditional practice session. Barkley emerged from this past Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers with a neck injury and an illness, but neither health concern looks like it will prevent him from playing Thursday in Dallas.
injuryReports.injury: The Eagles listed Barkley (neck/illness) as a full participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.

injuryReports.name: Byron Young
injuryReports.returnComment: Young had a productive outing in the victory, logging his first two sacks of the campaign. The 26-year-old will look to build on this strong performance and keep producing during the Week 12 matchup against the Cowboys.
injuryReports.injury: Young tallied four tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, during Philadelphia's win over the Steelers on Sunday

injuryReports.name: Jeremiah Trotter Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Trotter had a strong outing in the win, leading the team in tackles while playing every defensive snap. The 23-year-old has now tallied double-digit tackles in three straight games and will look to keep producing during Thursday's matchup versus the Cowboys.
injuryReports.injury: Trotter logged 13 tackles (nine solo) during Philadelphia's win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jaydon Blue
injuryReports.returnComment: The loose ball was recovered by the Steelers, and Pittsburgh's offense turned that takeaway into a 40-yard field goal by Chris Boswell four plays later. It ended up being the only touch of the game for Blue, who played all 11 of his snaps on special teams. There's an outside chance he sees some involvement on offense against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day, but that will depend on the availability of both Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) and Will Shipley (foot/illness).
injuryReports.injury: Blue returned his lone kickoff for 23 yards but fumbled the ball in the process during the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Eli Stowers
injuryReports.returnComment: Dallas Goedert (47 snaps), Johnny Mundt (eight) and Zach Ertz (six) handled tight-end duties for Philly, while Stowers played 20 snaps on special teams. The rookie tight end is miles from fantasy relevance this season.
injuryReports.injury: Stowers didn't log any offensive snaps in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Darius Cooper
injuryReports.returnComment: Cooper played 46 offensive snaps and 15 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver continues to see a significant snap share for the Eagles, drawing two more targets than rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon in the Week 11 win.
injuryReports.injury: Cooper caught four of his five targets for 59 yards in the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jake Elliott
injuryReports.returnComment: The Eagles kicker accounted for 13 of the team's 19 points, as he was good from 41, 29, 53 and 55 yards on his field goals. It was Elliott's first game with multiple field goals made since Week 4 against the Rams. That's how broken the Philadelphia offense has been for an extended period, and it doesn't project to get any better moving forward with Joe Milton at the controls. Elliott will be a hold-your-nose fantasy play in a theoretically high-scoring environment Thursday against the Cowboys, but it will be a movable force against a stoppable object when the Dallas defense squares off with the Eagles offense.
injuryReports.injury: Elliott went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his lone PAT in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Makai Lemon
injuryReports.returnComment: Lemon turned three targets into just three yards while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) paced the Eagles with 12 targets in the latter's return. In five games playing alongside Smith, Lemon has just 11 catches for 60 yards. Opportunities should be available against Dallas' porous secondary on Thanksgiving, but it remains to be seen if the unproven QB-WR combo of Joe Milton and Lemon can capitalize on that favorable matchup.
injuryReports.injury: Lemon caught one of three targets for three yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Joe Milton
injuryReports.returnComment: Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass or interception through two starts. He rushed for just seven yards Sunday after notching 64 rushing yards against the Giants in his first start with the Eagles, but Milton avoided mistakes as the Eagles rode their defense and Saquon Barkley's legs to their third win of the season. Twelve of Milton's 21 passes were directed to DeVonta Smith (hamstring) in their first game together. Milton is poised to start on Thanksgiving against the Cowboys, with whom he appeared in four games last season. He was on Dallas' practice squad prior to signing with the Eagles in October.
injuryReports.injury: Milton completed 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards while rushing five times for seven yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: DeVonta Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith was targeted on 12 of Joe Milton's 21 passes in the wide receiver's first game since Week 6. Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass through two starts for the Eagles, so expectations should be tempered for the team's passing game as a whole, but Smith has reclaimed his role as the team's top pass catcher. Smith could make the most of his hefty target share Thursday against the generous Dallas secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Smith (hamstring) caught five of 12 targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Cole Payton
injuryReports.returnComment: As the emergency third quarterback, Payton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both starter Joe Milton and backup Tanner McKee are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Payton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback against the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter informed the Eagles' medical staff while he was traveling to the stadium Sunday that his quadriceps was bothering him. The fifth-year defensive tackle has been cleared to suit up, but if he plays under a snap count or is available only as an emergency option, then Ty Robinson and Gabe Hall would be poised to take on larger roles on defense.
injuryReports.injury: Carter (quadriceps) is active for Sunday's game against the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Zack Baun
injuryReports.returnComment: Baun was held out of practice all week due to a back injury that he sustained against the Giants in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to require a stint on IR, which means he'll miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Seahawks. Jeremiah Trotter figures to start alongside Jihaad Campbell at inside linebacker moving forward, beginning with Sunday's home tilt against the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Dontayvion Wicks
injuryReports.returnComment: Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Wicks sustained the foot injury Friday, and it presumably led to his placement on IR. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Michael Carter II
injuryReports.returnComment: An abdominal injury prevented Carter from playing in Week 9 against the Giants. He had extra rest thanks to the Week 10 bye, and his full practice Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. Carter's return gives the Eagles a boost in the secondary and another contributor on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Carter (abdomen) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Nolan Smith Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: An illness limited Smith's practice reps both Wednesday and Thursday, but he was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. The fourth-year edge rusher has 17 tackles (nine solo), including 5.0 sacks, and one pass defense across eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Smith (illness) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Mason Rudolph
injuryReports.returnComment: Late Tuesday, the Steelers opted to make a change under center, naming Rudolph the Week 12 starter and sending Rodgers to the bench on the heels of poor performances by the offense in back-to-back losses to the Bengals and Eagles coming out of a bye week. The Steelers initially planned to make Rodgers inactive for Week 12 but keep him on the roster, but the team now intends to part ways with the four-time MVP after he harshly criticized head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday. The impending departure of Rodgers should thus give Rudolph an extended leash as the Steelers' starter, with a pair of inexperienced quarterbacks in second-year man Will Howard and rookie third-round pick Drew Allar representing the other options behind him on the depth chart. Over 38 career appearances (19 starts), the 31-year-old Rudolph has completed 64.2 percent of his passes for 6.6 yards per attempt and a 30:22 TD:INT.
injuryReports.injury: Rudolph will start Friday's game against the Broncos and could remain atop the depth chart for the rest of the season with the Steelers waiving Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Pittman also logged a full participation listing one day before, but the Steelers held a walkthrough practice Tuesday, so Wednesday's session is more relevant with regard to the WR's availability for Friday's game against the Broncos. If Pittman -- who last saw game action in Week 4 -- is activated to face Denver, he'll be catching passing in Week 12 from Mason Rudolph, with the Steelers slated to let veteran signal-calller Aaron Rodgers go.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: DeShon Elliott
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Cole Holcomb
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Heel

injuryReports.name: Gennings Dunker
injuryReports.returnComment: Dunker has put together four consecutive full sessions since being designated to return from injured reserve this past Wednesday. The rookie third-rounder is in the final stages of his recovery from an MCL sprain that he sustained in September. Dunker would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Friday's game against the Broncos.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jalen Ramsey
injuryReports.returnComment: Ramsey matched his season low in takedowns, but he was able to notch his first pass defensed since Week 5. The 32-year-old will have a chance to bounce back on a short week, taking on the Broncos on Friday at home.
injuryReports.injury: Ramsey recorded one solo tackle and a pass defensed during Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Patrick Queen
injuryReports.returnComment: Queen entered Week 11 having notched double-digit tackles in three straight games, but his streak was snapped versus Philadelphia. The linebacker has now compiled 78 total tackles (28 solo), including 3.5 sacks, four passes defensed, one of which is an interception, and a forced fumble over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Queen recorded four total tackles (three solo) during Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Nick Herbig
injuryReports.returnComment: Herbig upgraded his DNP practice status from last week to limited participation Tuesday. The 25-year-old missed Week 11 due to a hip injury. He has two more practice sessions to increase his chances of playing Friday against the Broncos.
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: Ben Skowronek
injuryReports.returnComment: The 29-year-old appears to have suffered a setback with his calf injury, as he opened Week 12 as a non-participant in practice Tuesday. Skowronek missed the Steelers' last three games due to the same injury. He will likely need to upgrade his practice status for a chance to play Friday against the Broncos.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Payton Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: One week after piling up 19 tackles (nine solo) in a loss to the Bengals, Wilson's three tackles Sunday were his fewest in a game this season. His 83 percent snap share on defense was also his lowest since Week 4. Wilson will be in position to rebound against Denver on Friday. He has 91 tackles (46 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and a fumble recovery across 10 games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson recorded just three tackles (one solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Roman Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: It was Wilson's first game since suffering a finger injury in Week 5 that landed him on injured reserve. He ended up playing 49 of 71 offensive snaps, 39 of which came out wide. Wilson had primarily operated as the Steelers' slot receiver prior to his injury, but Germie Bernard has emerged in that role for Pittsburgh. While Michael Pittman (foot) is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, DK Metcalf might receive some form of team-imposed discipline after he had an on-field meltdown against the Eagles before being ejected from the game.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson caught three of six targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Germie Bernard
injuryReports.returnComment: With Michael Pittman (foot) remaining sidelined for Week 11, Bernard retained his every-down role on offense, playing 67 of 71 offensive snaps while leading the team in routes (52) and targets. It was a nice bounce-back game for the rookie after he was held without a catch on three targets against the Bengals in Week 10. Pittman is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, but Bernard could keep pacing the team in playing time, especially if DK Metcalf gets disciplined for his latest on-field outburst.
injuryReports.injury: Bernard caught six passes for 40 yards on 10 targets in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Max Hurleman
injuryReports.returnComment: With DK Metcalf ejected in the second half of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles, Hurleman ended up playing 22 of 71 offensive snaps after getting bumped up from the practice squad to make his NFL debut. The  25-year-old saw seven targets, finishing with six receptions for 61 yards and the Steelers' lone touchdown of the contest. He also displaced Kaden Wetjen on the Steelers' return units, bringing back two kickoffs for 32 yards and three punts for 36 yards. Expect Hurleman to get elevated from the practice squad again in Friday's game against the Broncos.
injuryReports.injury: Hurleman reverted to the Steelers' practice squad Monday.

injuryReports.name: DK Metcalf
injuryReports.returnComment: Metcalf was disqualified with 4:53 remaining in the third quarter Sunday after he attempted to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye. He was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct in what was his second major transgression of the game; Metcalf previously drew an unnecessary roughness penalty in the first half, when he held his block of DeJean well after a play had finished. Though Metcalf won't miss further game action as a result of his ejection, he may have already lost the faith of his fantasy managers heading into a Week 12 matchup with the Broncos on Friday. Metcalf has hauled in just 36 of his 74 targets (48.6 percent catch rate) and has scored just two touchdowns on the season while topping 60 receiving yards in only two of his 10 appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Metcalf won't receive a suspension after he was ejected from Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles, but the NFL is still reviewing discipline for the receiver that could include a fine, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Alex Highsmith
injuryReports.returnComment: Highsmith recorded a pair of sacks across just six snaps before he was forced out in the first quarter of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles due to the ankle injury. Per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com, the Steelers' initial belief is that Highsmith's ankle injury isn't serious, but the edge rusher will nonetheless have difficulty getting clearance to play on a short week. If healthy, Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) -- who was inactive for Week 11 -- will be the most likely candidate to start in place of Highsmith on Friday.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Chris Boswell
injuryReports.returnComment: This was a battle of Pennsylvania's kickers, as Boswell and Jake Elliott combined to account for 23 of the game's 35 points. Boswell was good from 25, 40 and 52 yards. The veteran kicker has been trending downward the last two seasons, and he entered play Sunday having made just 79.2 percent of his field-goal tries this season. After his perfect showing against the Eagles, Boswell has made all of his field goals in back-to-back games for the first time all season. On the year, he's 22-for-27 on FGAs and a perfect 18-for-18 on PATs.
injuryReports.injury: Boswell went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his lone PAT in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Darnell Washington
injuryReports.returnComment: The big tight end earned just a 6.8 percent target share on a day when Aaron Rodgers fired off 44 pass attempts in prolonged comeback mode. Washington has been held to 25 yards or fewer in eight of 10 games this season. He doesn't see enough volume to warrant weekly fantasy consideration as a touchdown-or-bust bet.
injuryReports.injury: Washington caught all three targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Pat Freiermuth
injuryReports.returnComment: Freiermuth matched his season high in catches, securing five passes in a game for the third time this year. The tight end has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards in a contest this season, and he entered Week 11 with exactly two catches in each of the team's last four games. Freiermuth has now caught 32 of 43 targets for 309 yards and five touchdowns while also adding four rushes for five yards and a score over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 39 yards during Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Rico Dowdle
injuryReports.returnComment: Dowdle finished with 34 scrimmage yards for a second consecutive game after racking up 235 scrimmage yards over his preceding four appearances. He had five more yards than Jaylen Warren on two fewer touches in Sunday's loss. Dowdle is poised to retain his spot as the 1B option alongside Warren in Friday's Week 12 home game against the Broncos.
injuryReports.injury: Dowdle rushed five times for 15 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Warren
injuryReports.returnComment: Warren finished with 29 yards on 11 touches compared to 34 yards on nine touches for Rico Dowdle, as Pittsburgh's backfield duo was held quiet for a second consecutive game. After recording at least 73 scrimmage yards in eight consecutive games to start the season, Warren has produced just 75 yards without a touchdown over the past two games. Warren and Dowdle should continue to split backfield touches Friday against the Broncos.
injuryReports.injury: Warren rushed nine times for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for one yard in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Kaden Wetjen
injuryReports.returnComment: Wetjen has operated as the Steelers' top returner on both kickoffs and punts this season. However, with Roman Wilson back from injured reserve and Max Hurleman elevated from the practice squad to the active roster, Wetjen will be a healthy scratch Sunday for the first time this season. Wetjen's next opportunity to play is Friday against the Broncos, although the rookie fourth-rounder's chances of suiting up for that contest would be further diminished if Michael Pittman (foot) is activated from IR before that game.
injuryReports.injury: Wetjen (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles.

injuryReports.name: Sam Okuayinonu
injuryReports.returnComment: Okuayinonu suffered a broken foot in practice ahead of Week 1 and required surgery. He appears to be making progress and could return at some point before the end of the regular season. The 28-year-old appeared in 15 regular-season games last season, making 12 starts, and recorded 23 tackles (16 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Nate Hobbs
injuryReports.returnComment: San Francisco needed to make a decision on Hobbs after his 21-day practice window was set to close. The veteran cornerback will be looking to make his 2026 debut Sunday against the Seahawks.
injuryReports.injury: The 49ers activated Hobbs (groin) from injured reserve Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
injuryReports.returnComment: Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Mike Evans
injuryReports.returnComment: After a three-game (and four-week) absence due to right Achilles tendinitis, Evans returned to action during Sunday's win against the Vikings in Mexico City, recording a 43-percent snap share and gathering in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown. The 49ers likely are managing Evans' workload to begin Week 12 prep, but his status nonetheless will be monitored in advance of Sunday's contest against the Seahawks.
injuryReports.injury: Achilles

injuryReports.name: Brock Purdy
injuryReports.returnComment: Purdy put on a master class during this past Sunday's 35-10 win against the Vikings in Mexico City, completing 21 of 26 passes for 255 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. Now with a health concern in tow, his status will be monitored closely to get a sense of his odds to suit up Sunday against the Seahawks. Mac Jones is waiting in the wings in the even Purdy isn't able to play in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Colton McKivitz
injuryReports.returnComment: ir
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Brayden Willis
injuryReports.returnComment: Willis has suited up in each of the 49ers' last nine games but has received little run on offense while the team's top two tight ends -- George Kittle and Luke Farrell -- have maintained health throughout the season. The 27-year-old has logged single-digit snaps on offense in five straight contests and has yet to draw a target in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Willis went without a target while logging nine snaps on offense and 21 on special teams in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Luke Farrell
injuryReports.returnComment: Farrell has suited up in each of the 49ers' first 10 games, but despite logging double-digit snaps in each contest, he's produced just four catches for 40 yards on seven targets. He'll continue to serve mainly as a blocking tight end on offense while also serving as a key contributor on the 49ers' special-teams units.
injuryReports.injury: Farrell turned his lone target into a seven-yard reception in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Ji'Ayir Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown picked off a pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tai Felton late in the second quarter, which Brown returned 18 yards to the house to extend the 49ers' lead to 28-10. It was his first interception of 2026 and sixth of his career, and Brown is up to 55 tackles (31 solo) and four pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Brown recorded four tackles (three solo) and a pick-six during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings on Sunday in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Khalid Kareem
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Dre Greenlaw
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Fred Warner
injuryReports.returnComment: The four-time First-Team All-Pro linebacker has double-digit tackles in five of 10 games this season and is up to 96 tackles (42 solo), including 0.5 sacks, five forced fumbles, four pass breakups and a fumble recovery on 96 percent of the Niners' defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Warner recorded eight tackles (four solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Cowing
injuryReports.returnComment: Cowing saw limited action in the win, playing just six snaps on offense and two on special teams. The 25-year-old hasn't been targeted across the last two games and should continue to serve a depth role with Mike Evans now healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Cowing returned one punt for no gain during San Francisco's win over the Vikings on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jordan James
injuryReports.returnComment: James went without a touch on offense for the majority of the game, but he was able to turn the team's final two carries of the game into seven yards late in the fourth quarter. The running back was on the field for five offensive plays, and he'll remain the team's No. 3 option behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black in Week 12 against the Seahawks.
injuryReports.injury: James rushed twice for seven yards during Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Juszczyk
injuryReports.returnComment: Juszczyk was able to reel in his first two passes since Week 7, notching his fourth multi-catch performance of the year. The fullback has now caught 10 of 13 targets for 89 yards and two touchdowns while also adding a four-yard rush over nine contests to open the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Juszczyk caught both of his targets for 13 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Watkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Watkins' 28 offensive snaps were tied with Deebo Samuel for second most among 49ers wide receivers behind Keenan Allen (31) and ahead of Mike Evans (23). Watkins has played at least 50 percent of San Francisco's offensive snaps in each of the team's last five games, but the second-year pro is stuck in a complementary role on offense behind Evans, Allen, Samuel, tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey. The 49ers travel back home for a critical Week 12 tilt against the Seahawks on Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Watkins brought in his lone target for 19 yards during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Eddy Pineiro
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the veteran kicker's third game this season that he didn't attempt a field goal, but he's now gone three straight games with exactly five extra points. Pineiro now leads the league in both point-after attempts (40) and makes (36), but he's attempted just 11 field goals in a highly efficient San Francisco offense. The lack of field goals certainly keeps him from being a top fantasy kicker.
injuryReports.injury: Pineiro made all five of his PATs in Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Deommodore Lenoir
injuryReports.returnComment: Lenoir played in Week 11 despite working through a foot injury that was sustained in Week 9 against Las Vegas. The issue didn't seem to slow the 27-year-old against the Vikings, as he played 81.0 percent of defensive snaps, which was within his usual range.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Keenan Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Sunday marked Allen's first time working with Mike Evans, the 49ers' top wide receiver, and the latter dominated the attention of QB Brock Purdy, posting a 6-109-1 line on seven targets in his first game action since Week 6. If Evans' Achilles issue flares up at any point, Allen may be thrust into WR1 duties, which could yield more consistent results as he becomes more acclimated to head coach Kyle Shanahan's offense. For now, though, Allen will play a distant second to Evans for as long as the latter is healthy and available.
injuryReports.injury: Allen totaled three catches (on four targets) for 38 yards during Sunday's 35-10 victory against the Vikings in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Kaelon Black
injuryReports.returnComment: Black entered Week 11 action on the heels of three consecutive contests with double-digit touches, so Sunday's performance was a step back to his modest outings from Weeks 2-6. In any case, the rookie third-round pick continues to be utilized regularly in the 49ers offense, averaging 9.1 touches for 37.8 yards from scrimmage per game while working as the clear No. 2 RB behind Christian McCaffrey. Black's next chance to contribute arrives next Sunday against the Seahawks.
injuryReports.injury: Black notched six carries for eight yards and secured his only target for seven yards during Sunday's 35-10 win versus the Vikings in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Samuel didn't come close to replicating the 109 yards from scrimmage and two TDs on six touches that he accrued during a Week 10 shootout in Dallas, but he continued to mix into the offense in all realms, as he's ranged from two to eight touches in each of his seven appearances this season. Overall, he's averaging 11.7 yards per catch and a whopping 13.1 yards per carry to go with five total touchdowns in 2026, making him one big play away from producing weekly.
injuryReports.injury: Samuel logged two carries for 27 yards, gathered in three of four targets for 20 yards and returned two kickoffs for 57 yards during Sunday's 35-10 win against the Vikings in Mexico City.

injuryReports.name: George Kittle
injuryReports.returnComment: Kittle scored on both of his first-half catches, capping San Francisco's opening drive with a 17-yard touchdown before adding an eight-yard score in the first minute of the second quarter. The multi-touchdown performance was especially impressive considering the Vikings came in having allowed just one touchdown on a league-low 33 catches to tight ends. Kittle has been one of the top performers at his position as usual, with seven touchdown catches in 10 games, though his streak of consecutive outings with at least four catches ended at eight games. Up next for Kittle is a Week 12 home game against the Seahawks.
injuryReports.injury: Kittle caught all three of his targets for 34 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Christian McCaffrey
injuryReports.returnComment: McCaffrey was relatively quiet in the lopsided win, but he extended his touchdown streak to nine games with a six-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. The versatile running back was much less involved as a pass catcher Sunday night after racking up 161 yards and two touchdowns through the air against the Cowboys in Week 10, and he finished with a season-low 62 scrimmage yards against the Vikings. Backup Kaelon Black had just eight rushing yards on his six carries after siphoning off at least 11 rushing attempts in each of the previous three games. McCaffrey is set to face another stout defensive front in Week 12 when the 49ers host the Seahawks, against whom McCaffrey churned out 83 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 5.
injuryReports.injury: McCaffrey rushed 12 times for 49 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for 13 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith-Njigba previously has been listed on Seattle injury reports this season for rest purposes, but this marks the first time his practice reps were impacted by a health concern. He'll have two more days to increase his activity level this week, with Friday's practice report set to reveal if he has a designation for Sunday's game at San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Abraham Lucas
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Quenton Nelson
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Sam Darnold
injuryReports.returnComment: Darnold missed the Seahawks' last two games while tending to a pair of injuries, but he appears to be feeling healthier coming out of a Week 11 bye. While Macdonald stopped just short of confirming him the team's Week 12 starter, Darnold should get the nod if he's able to practice without restrictions Wednesday and occurs no setbacks along the way.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Leonard Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Charles Cross
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: George Holani
injuryReports.returnComment: Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - MCL

injuryReports.name: Devon Witherspoon
injuryReports.returnComment: Coach Mike MacDonald dialed up the blitz against rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza in his first career start. Two of Witherspoon's four tackles in the Seahawks' win came behind the line of scrimmage off cornerback blitzes against Mendoza. Witherspoon also played all 59 of the team's defensive snaps in the one-score win.
injuryReports.injury: Witherspoon logged four solo tackles, including 2.0 sacks, in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Ernest Jones IV
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones helped make first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza's NFL debut miserable. The inside linebacker helped the Seahawks' defense contain the young quarterback's scrambling ability while also limiting his mid-range opportunities from the pocket en route to yet another defensive win for the defending champs.
injuryReports.injury: Jones logged 10 tackles (five solo) in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jason Myers
injuryReports.returnComment: Myers missed a 44-yard field-goal attempt with 7:05 remaining in the game that would have put the Seahawks up 14 points. The kicker is now 16-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 21-for-23 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Myers missed his sole field-goal attempt and made three PATs in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Cooper Kupp
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Kupp hauled in his lone target for a 34-yard touchdown during the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tory Horton
injuryReports.returnComment: Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.
injuryReports.injury: Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: AJ Barner
injuryReports.returnComment: Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.
injuryReports.injury: Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Rashid Shaheed
injuryReports.returnComment: After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.
injuryReports.injury: Shaheed caught one pass for eight yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Drew Lock
injuryReports.returnComment: Lock took advantage of having WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba at his disposal, targeting him 10 times, one of which resulted in a 71-yard TD connection. Moreover, Lock also hooked up with Cooper Kupp on a sliding 34-yard touchdown, marking his second multi-TD outing in four appearances (three starts) this season. There's an expectation that Seahawks No. 1 QB Sam Darnold (quadriceps) returns from a two-game absence after the team's Week 11 bye, but until he receives a clean bill of health, Lock has a chance to be under center on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Lock completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and logged six carries for 20 yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory in Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: Jadarian Price
injuryReports.returnComment: This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: Zach Charbonnet
injuryReports.returnComment: Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Charbonnet churned out 94 yards on 20 carries during Sunday's 21-13 win in Las Vegas.
